question.problem:
$$
A=[\begin{aligned}2 & 4 \\ -1 & 1 \\ 2 & 1\end{aligned}],\,B=\{[\begin{aligned}2 \\ -1 \\ 2\end{aligned}],[\begin{aligned}a \\ b \\ c\end{aligned}]\}
$$

Consider the subspace $\text{Col}(A)$ and an orthogonal basis $B$ of $\text{Col}(A),$ where $A$ and $B$ are given above. Given that $B$ is derived from $\text{Col}(A)$ using the Gram-Schmidt process, what is the value of $\frac{a}{c}?$

Consider the subspace $\textrm{Col}(A)$ and an orthogonal basis $\mathcal B$ of $\textrm{Col}(A),$ where $A$ and $\mathcal B$ are given below. Given that $\mathcal B$ is derived from $\textrm{Col}(A)$ using the Gram-Schmidt process, what is the value of $\dfrac{c}{a}?$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14157663/assets/0bd5963e6d7aa7c67fe46f8775cb21270e0ce04b3a36f0345f1635acf58a9eb5.svg)
current_example.worked_solution:
Recall that $\textrm{Col}(A)$ is the span of the columns of $A.$  

First, let's denote

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14157663/assets/849c0c0fe35fb26bc2c53c7db542e03011f909ca92f24114350935038e87dfdd.svg)

We proceed to find an orthogonal basis using the Gram-Schmidt process, as follows.

- **Step 1**: We set ![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14157663/assets/a0c98defdedb2f43a0ccde2c41f54be5f67ab60b2973f0755ae64fd9fc0b92a4.svg)

- **Step 2**: Next, we find $\mathbf{v}_2$, by using the formula

$$
\begin{aligned}{v}_{2} & ={a}_{2}-\frac{{a}_{2}\cdot {v}_{1}}{{v}_{1}\cdot {v}_{1}}{v}_{1}.\end{aligned}
$$

Applying the formula for $\mathbf v_2$ in our case gives

$$
\begin{aligned}{v}_{2} & ={a}_{2}-\frac{(-5)\cdot 1+(-1)\cdot (-2)+(-3)\cdot 2}{{1}^{2}+(-2)^{2}+{2}^{2}}{v}_{1} \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-5 \\ -1 \\ -3\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -2 \\ 2\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-4 \\ -3 \\ -1\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, ![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14157663/assets/ff7f9403f52042c0fb0db0647c3746094baa8764da7b11aae6bf4106a1c37c16.svg) is an orthogonal basis for $\textrm{Col}(A).$

Finally, $a=-4,$ $c=-1,$ and  

$$
\dfrac{c}{a} = \dfrac{-1}{-4} = \dfrac{1}{4}.
$$
